title: Krishna and the Mountain
bigQuestion: How can we share and keep others safe?

story.title: A Hill Like an Umbrella
story.kicker: Rain pours for days, and a boy holds up a whole hill on one finger.
paragraphs: Rain falls on the little village. It falls and falls. The cows moo. The children shiver. Water fills the paths between the houses.
A cowherd boy looks at the big hill nearby. His name is Krishna. "Come with me," he tells everyone. "I will keep you safe."
Krishna lifts the whole hill! He holds it up on one small finger. It is like a giant umbrella. People and cows crowd under it, warm and dry.
Many Hindus love this story. They tell it to their children again and again. It is one of many stories about Krishna as a boy.
story.think: Krishna kept everyone safe. Who keeps you safe when it storms?

lessons.title: A Boy in a Cowherd Village
lessons.mainIdea: Krishna grows up in a village of cowherds.
reading: *Krishna* grows up in a small village. The people there care for cows. They are called cowherds.
His mother is Yashoda. She loves him very much. Many Hindus honor Krishna as a form of God. They love the stories of his childhood.

words.d: a cowherd boy in the stories, honored by many Hindus as a form of God
a person who takes care of cows

look.title: Morning in the Village
look.text: Look at the village in the morning. Cows walk to the green fields. Children run beside them. A little blue boy plays a flute. The cows turn to listen.
look.prompt: What sounds might you hear in this village?

check.q: Where does Krishna grow up?
check.why: The stories say Krishna grew up in a village of cowherds.

check.q: Who is Krishna's mother in these stories?
check.why: Yashoda raises Krishna in the village.

check.q: What does a cowherd do?
check.why: A cowherd takes care of cows.

lessons.title: The Butter Pot
lessons.mainIdea: Little Krishna loves butter, and families smile at his tricks.
reading: Yashoda makes fresh butter. She keeps it in a clay pot. Little Krishna loves butter. He sneaks some from the pot!
His friends help him reach it. Yashoda finds butter on his face. She is cross, but she loves him. Families smile at this story.

words.d: a soft, rich food made from milk

look.title: The Boy Who Loved Butter
look.text: Little Krishna takes butter from the pots and shares it with his friends and even the monkeys. Yashoda tries to catch him.
look.cite: Retold from the Bhagavata Purana, Book 10, chapters 8 and 9
look.prompt: Krishna shares the butter. Who does he share it with?

check.q: What does little Krishna love to eat?
check.why: The stories say little Krishna loves butter.

check.q: Where does Yashoda keep the butter?
check.why: Yashoda keeps the butter in a clay pot.

check.q: How does Yashoda feel about Krishna?
check.why: Yashoda is cross, but she loves Krishna very much.

lessons.title: Sharing With Friends
lessons.mainIdea: Krishna shares what he has with his friends.
reading: Krishna does not keep the butter all to himself. He shares it with his friends. Everyone gets a taste.
Many families tell this part on purpose. It helps children think about sharing. Sharing makes friends happy.

words.d: to give some of what you have to others

look.title: One Snack, Many Friends
look.text: Look at the boy with a bowl of butter. Four friends sit near him. He gives each friend a scoop. They all laugh together.
look.prompt: Tell about a time you shared something. How did it feel?

check.q: What does Krishna do with the butter?
check.why: In the stories, Krishna shares the butter with his friends.

check.q: What does share mean?
check.why: To share is to give some of what you have to others.

check.q: Why do families tell the sharing part?
choices: To help children think about sharing
check.why: Families use the story to talk about sharing.

lessons.title: Rain and Wind
lessons.mainIdea: A huge storm comes to Krishna's village.
reading: One day dark clouds come. Rain pours down. The wind blows hard. It rains for days and days.
The story says Indra, king of the sky, sent the storm. The people and cows are cold and afraid. They need a safe place.

look.title: Stormy Sky
look.text: Look at the gray sky. Rain comes down like long strings. Trees bend in the wind. A calf hides behind its mother.
look.prompt: What do you do to stay safe in a storm?

check.q: What comes to the village?
check.why: A huge storm comes to the village.

check.q: Who does the story say sent the storm?
check.why: The story says Indra sent the storm.

check.q: How do the people feel?
check.why: The people and cows are cold and afraid in the storm.

lessons.title: Lifting Govardhan Hill
lessons.mainIdea: Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill to keep everyone safe.
reading: Krishna walks to Govardhan Hill. He lifts it up with one hand. He holds it on one finger!
Everyone runs under the hill. The cows come too. They stay dry for seven days. Then the storm stops.

words.d: the hill Krishna lifts in the story

look.title: Seven Days Under the Hill
look.text: Krishna holds up the hill for seven days. The people and cows rest under it. When the rain stops, they all come out safe.
look.cite: Retold from the Bhagavata Purana, Book 10, chapter 25
look.prompt: How long does Krishna hold up the hill?

check.q: What does Krishna lift?
check.why: Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill in the story.

check.q: What is the hill like?
check.why: The hill keeps the rain off like a giant umbrella.

check.q: How long do they stay under the hill?
check.why: The Bhagavata Purana says Krishna held the hill for seven days.

lessons.title: Janmashtami
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus celebrate Krishna's birthday at Janmashtami.
reading: Janmashtami is Krishna's birthday festival. It comes in late summer. Many Hindu families celebrate it.
Some families stay up until midnight. The stories say Krishna was born at midnight. Some rock a little cradle. They sing songs about baby Krishna.

look.title: A Tiny Cradle
look.text: Look at the home shrine. A tiny cradle has flowers all around it. A family sings softly. A clock shows it is almost midnight.
look.prompt: Why do you think the family waits until midnight?

check.q: What is Janmashtami?
check.why: Janmashtami celebrates Krishna's birthday.

check.q: When do the stories say Krishna was born?
check.why: The stories say Krishna was born at midnight.

check.q: What do some families rock?
check.why: Some families rock a little cradle for baby Krishna.

lessons.title: Stories at Home
lessons.mainIdea: Families tell Krishna stories to share what they value.
reading: Families tell Krishna stories at Janmashtami. They tell about the butter. They tell about the hill.
The stories help children talk about big ideas. Share with others. Keep others safe. Hindu families in Illinois tell them too.

words.d: a special day or days when people celebrate together
